text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The government, trade unions and the employers association Confindustria discussed the 11.5 trillion lire Euro-tax. The government initially planned to collect 8.5 trillion lire from additional income taxes but reportedly agreed to lower the target to 5.5 trillion lire (all).
* President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro said, "Here there is no dictatorship" after the centre-right bloc denounced a "red alert" for Italian democracy.(all).
* The government might nominate today the successor of resigning Public Works minister Antonio Di Pietro (all).

* Many visitors, including leftist politicians and Foreign minister Lamberto Dini, went for talks or to pay homage to Cuban leader Fidel Castro in Rome. Castro is expected to pay a historic visit to Pope Jean Paul II today (all).

* At least five candidates declared a preliminary interest in the sale of loss-making Banco di Napoli: state-controlled Banca Nazionale del Lavoro and insurer INA, who are presenting a common offer, the Treasury-owned bank Mediocredito centrale, and two unnamed foreign investors. Natwest (GB), Bayerische landerbank (Germany) and Rabobank (Netherlands) are reportedly interested (all).
* Italy's September producer prices rose 0.2 percent year-on-year (all).
* In the first nine months of 1996 pre-tax profits for carmaker Fiat fell to 1.759 trillion lire from 2.743 trillion lire while its sales rose 4 percent to 57.918 trillion lire (all).
* Italian debt futures hit a new historic high at 128.38 (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
